rows.speaker: مروان بن الحكم والمسور بن مخرمة
rows.claim: At Hudaybiyya, Khuzaa joined Muhammad’s pact and Banu Bakr joined Quraysh; after seventeen or eighteen months, Banu Bakr attacked Khuzaa at al-Watir.
rows.anchor: عن مروان بن الحكم والمسور بن مخرمة قالا كان في صلح رسول الله

rows.speaker: مروان بن الحكم والمسور بن مخرمة
rows.claim: Quraysh secretly assisted Banu Bakr with mounts and weapons because of hostility toward the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فأعانوهم عليهم بالكراع والسلاح فقاتلوهم معهم للضغن على رسول الله

rows.speaker: عمرو بن سالم
rows.claim: Amr ibn Salim rode to Medina and recited an appeal for the Prophet to honor the ancestral alliance and aid Khuzaa.
rows.anchor: وركب عمرو بن سالم عندما كان من أمر خزاعة وبني بكر بالوتير حتى قدم المدينة على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بأبيات

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet promised Amr support, treated a passing cloud as witness to victory for Banu Ka‘b, and ordered an expedition while concealing its destination.
rows.anchor: نصرت يا عمرو بن سالم فما برح حتى مرت غمامة في السماء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: Their reports identify Quraysh’s breach and aid to Banu Bakr against Khuzaa as the occasion for the command to fight through the promise to heal believers’ hearts.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد وعكرمة أن قصة نقض قريش عهد الحديبية وإعانتهم بني بكر على خزاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Hudaybiyya account explains these verses, their contextual wording places them before the conquest of Mecca and before the verses of Bara’a.
rows.anchor: على ما يعطيه السياق مما نزل قبل فتح مكة فتكون نازلة قبل آيات براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and al-Bayhaqi’s account, despite including al-Miswar ibn Makhrama, does not expressly say the verses were revealed on that occasion.
rows.anchor: لا تصرح بنزول الآيات في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The occasion reports attributed to Mujahid and Ikrima are not dependable because they stop short and are disconnected.
rows.anchor: وما رواها مجاهد وعكرمة لا اعتماد عليه لمكان الوقف والانقطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage’s context still allows these verses to have been revealed together with, and connected to, the preceding verses.
rows.anchor: وسياق الآيات لا يأبى نزولها مع ما تقدم عليها واتصالها بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traits of oath-breaking and plotting the Messenger’s expulsion could describe Quraysh’s allied neighbors after the conquest, by association with Quraysh.
rows.anchor: من الجائز أن تكون الآية مشيرة إلى حلفاء قريش وجيرانهم ممن لم يؤمنوا بعد فتح مكة

rows.speaker: أهل البيت
rows.claim: Reports from the Prophet’s Household apply these verses to the advent of the Mahdi; al-Tabataba’i classifies this as the Qur’anic mode of jary.
rows.anchor: روايات متفرقة من طرق أهل البيت عليهم السلام تطبق الآيات على ظهور المهدي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human social thought represents material activities through imagined analogies to natural bodies and their laws, as names represent people and leaders represent heads.
rows.anchor: الإنسان في مسير حياته لا يزال يصور أعماله وما يتعلق به أعماله من المادة تصور الأمور الكونية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People make covenants to protect life and secure its benefits, since they seek enjoyment and ward off whatever obstructs it.
rows.anchor: العامل الأولي في ذلك أن الإنسان لا هم له إلا التحفظ على حياته والوصول إلى مزاياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most social work needs preparation before it can succeed: people must assemble means, remove obstacles, and ensure control over the time required.
rows.anchor: بعضها يتم بالسلطة المقصورة على الفعل مقدار زمانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A covenant secures cooperation or noninterference from other people, illustrated by coordinating labor to make clothing and protecting one’s occupancy of a home.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الذي هدى الإنسان إلى اعتبار العقد وإبرام العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion excludes named transactional contracts and concerns general promises of assistance or noninterference, for a term or indefinitely.
rows.anchor: الكلام في العهد بمعنى ما يعقده الإنسان لغيره من الإعانة أو عدم الممانعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a pact remains binding until one party or both parties breach it.
rows.anchor: وهو نوع أحكام وإبرام لا ينتقض إلا بنقض أحد الطرفين أو بنقضهما معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oaths and hand pledges intensify a covenant by placing the oath-taker’s sanctity or the pledger’s hand as a bond for performance.
rows.anchor: وربما زيد على إحكام العهد بالحلف وهو أن يقيد المعاهد ما يعطيه من العهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Society functions like a larger human being: its life and purposes depend on its members and it needs security from both them and other societies.
rows.anchor: فالمجتمع إنسان كبير له مقاصد الحياة ما للإنسان الصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human communities continually need pacts across political, economic, cultural, and other affairs to pursue their shared aims safely.
rows.anchor: فلم يزل ولا يزال المجتمع من المجتمعات الإنسانية في حاجة قائمة إلى أن يعاهد غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam legislates the community’s social affairs and treats breaking a covenant as a grave sin unless the other party first breaks it.
rows.anchor: والعهد الذي نتكلم فيه قد اعتبره اعتبارا تاما وأحكمه إحكاما يعد نقضه من طرف أهله من أكبر الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an commands fulfillment of covenants and condemns their breach, citing the command to fulfill contracts and the severe consequence of breaking God’s covenant.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الذين آمنوا أوفوا بالعقود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pact may be ended only in the interest of justice after betrayal or fear of betrayal, and the opposing party must be notified openly rather than ambushed.
rows.anchor: فانبذ إليهم على سواء إن الله لا يحب الخائنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the Muslim community renounces pacts with polytheists, it grants four months for reflection and free decision; the reprieve allowed some to believe and be saved.
rows.anchor: حتى يكونوا على مهل من التفكر في أمرهم والتروي في شأنهم فيروا رأيهم على حرية من الفكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A polytheist who seeks protection must be sheltered until hearing God’s speech, then escorted to safety, because the people do not know.
rows.anchor: وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله ثم أبلغه مأمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims must remain faithful to a pact with those who remain faithful; this is grounded in piety, which God loves.
rows.anchor: فما استقاموا لكم فاستقيموا لهم إن الله يحب المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who would show agreement verbally while their hearts refuse it are untrustworthy; most of them are transgressors.
rows.anchor: يرضونكم بأفواههم وتأبى قلوبهم وأكثرهم فاسقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to reciprocate an attack requires an equivalent response, not an excess.
rows.anchor: فمن اعتدى عليكم فاعتدوا عليه بمثل ما اعتدى عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hostility over exclusion from the Sacred Mosque cannot justify aggression; believers must cooperate in piety, not sin or aggression.
rows.anchor: ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم إن صدوكم عن المسجد الحرام أن تعتدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam does not permit initiating a breach of a treaty without the other party’s breach.
rows.anchor: وأما النقض الابتدائي من غير نقض من العدو المعاهد فلا مجوز له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet made treaties with Jewish tribes and Quraysh and broke them only after the other side breached its obligations.
rows.anchor: فقد عاهد بني قينقاع وبني قريظة وغيرهم من اليهود ولم ينقض إلا بعدما نقضوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hudaybiyya pact ended only after Quraysh helped Banu Bakr attack Khuzaa, allies of the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولم ينقض حتى نقضوا باظهار بني بكر على خزاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even lost advantages or harm do not justify breach when the community can defend itself or offer a plausible excuse; truth remains the governing standard.
rows.anchor: فإن مدار الأمر على الحق، والحق لا يستعقب شرا ولا ضرا إلا على من انحرف عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Materialist societies treat moral virtue as useful only when it benefits the community; treaties then track immediate interests and relative power, and the stronger party invents pretexts to abandon them.
rows.anchor: وما يعقد فيها من العهود والمواثيق إنما يعقد على حسب مصلحة الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In societies focused solely on material gain, lying, treachery, and aggression do not restrain the pursuit of perceived benefit; public history supplies examples.
rows.anchor: وأما الكذب أو الخيانة أو التعدي لما يتخذه الغير منافع لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam regards true life and happiness as joining material and spiritual well-being, and grounds law in human nature and truth rather than popular desire.
rows.anchor: وإنما يرى حياته الحقيقية حياته الجامعة بين المادة والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief, good character, and sound deeds must be honored even when they bring no material advantage, because they follow truth.
rows.anchor: فمن الواجب رعاية جانب الفضائل الإنسانية نفعت أو ضرت والتجنب عن الرذائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ends the polytheists’ pact for their breach but grants a reprieve, honors those who keep their pact, and requires notice before ending a pact for feared betrayal.
rows.anchor: وكذا يأمر نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إن خاف من قوم خيانة أن ينقض عهدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An act belongs both to its immediate cause and to the ultimate cause of that cause; relative to the latter, the near agent functions as an instrument.
rows.anchor: فللفعل نسبة إلى فاعله، وله انتساب إلى فاعل فاعله بعين هذه النسبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even consciousness and choice are given by the ultimate agent, so an act can be intended through the chosen action of an intermediary.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الاختيار لم يوجده الفاعل المختار لنفسه وإنما أوجده الفاعل الذي أوجد الفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary language truthfully attributes actions to near and remote agents; the author rejects calling remote-agent attribution metaphor merely because the agent did not act directly.
rows.anchor: وليس أصل النسبة إلا نسبة حقيقية من غير مجاز قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Actions whose meanings specify bodily execution, such as eating, drinking, or sitting, are attributed only to the immediate actor.
rows.anchor: فما كان منها يكشف بمفهومه عن خصوصيات المباشرة والاتصال بالعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Effects such as killing, capturing, reviving, giving, or honoring can be attributed equally to proximate and remote agents, sometimes more strongly to the more powerful remote agent.
rows.anchor: وأما الأعمال التي لا تعتبر فيها خصوصيات المباشرة والحركات المادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an attributes punishment carried out by believers’ hands to God, using their hands as instruments.
rows.anchor: قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم ويخزهم وينصركم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording of 37:96 can refer either to idols shaped by people or to their acts; in either reading, God’s creation is related to human work.
rows.anchor: والله خلقكم وما تعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creation is attributed even to the ships whose construction is human work, just as natural life-giving processes are attributed to God.
rows.anchor: ففيه نسبة الخلق إلى الفلك والفلك بما هي من عمل الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s causation and natural or human causes do not compete: they operate in a vertical order, which materialists confuse with mutually exclusive causes.
rows.anchor: ولا منافاة في جميع هذه الموارد بين انتساب الأمر إليه تعالى وانتسابه إلى غيره من الأسباب

rows.speaker: الأشاعرة
rows.claim: The Ash‘arites infer from God punishing unbelievers through believers’ hands that God creates human acts and people have no choice; the hands are mere instruments.
rows.anchor: استدلت الأشاعرة بقوله تعالى { قاتلوهم يعذبهم الله بأيديكم } الآية

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba’i argues that this would also attribute unbelievers’ killing believers, lying against prophets, and cursing believers to God, so human acts must be created by people.
rows.anchor: وأجاب عنه الجبائي من المعتزلة بأنه لو جاز أن يقال إن الله يعذب الكافرين بأيدي المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the Ash‘arites accept the implication of attributing vile acts to God in doctrine, though they avoid saying it aloud out of reverence.
rows.anchor: وأجاب عنه الرازي بأن أصحابنا يلتزمون جميع ما ألزم به الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ash‘arite position follows from denying real causality among created things and treating their apparent causal order as God’s habitual sequence alone.
rows.anchor: ما ذهبوا إليه من نفي رابطة العلية والمعلولية من بين الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying created causality removes the very basis for inferring God as cause; ordinary reasoning and practical life presume real cause and effect.
rows.anchor: وببطلانها يبطل ما أثبتوه من انحصار السببية فيه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an affirms causality, credits good to God, and excludes evil, frivolity, and blameworthy acts from Him.
rows.anchor: وينسب كل حسنة إليه تعالى وينفي استناد السيئات والمعاصي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Materialist determinists also deny human freedom, but because an action follows necessarily from its complete set of causes; the person and will alone are only part of that cause, so the action remains optional for them.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا نسبت إلى الإنسان وحده أو إلى الإنسان المريد فقد نسبت إلى جزء العلة التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ash‘arites and materialists confuse necessity relative to a complete cause with possibility relative to one causal part, which is the basis of human choice.
rows.anchor: فؤلاء خلطوا في كلامهم بين النسبتين فوضعوا النسبة الوجوبية التي للفعل إلى مجموع أجزاء علتها التامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mu‘tazili implication is valid, but its unacceptable consequence does not prove that human acts have no relation to God; one act is attributed vertically to both the direct agent and the creator of that agent.
rows.anchor: لجواز كونها منسوبة إليه تعالى بعين ما ينتسب به إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bodily action categories such as lawful or unlawful sex and eating belong to the human subject, while God creates the person without undergoing that motion; broader terms like guidance, trial, and punishment can apply to both.
rows.anchor: وأما عنوان الفعل الذي يشير إلى جهة قيام الحركة والسكون بالموضوع المتحرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer’s killing an unbeliever is God’s punishment of the unbeliever, while an unbeliever’s killing a believer is a trial for the believer.
rows.anchor: فقتل المؤمن للكافر تعذيب إلهي للكافر، وقتل الكافر للمؤمن بلاء حسن للمؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an declares God the creator of everything; human actions are truly attributable both to their direct human agents and, in a manner befitting God, to Him.
rows.anchor: ذلكم الله ربكم خالق كل شيء لا إله إلا هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s provision reaches both groups, supporting the layered attribution of acts without positing a second independent creator.
rows.anchor: كلا نمد هؤلاء وهؤلاء من عطاء ربك وما كان عطاء ربك محظورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse sets out three ordered proofs of divine lordship: one addressed through the idolaters’ own account of cosmic management, one through afterlife accountability, and one through the truth sought by spiritual elect.
rows.anchor: وهي ثلاث حجج مرتبة بحسب الدقة والمتانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first proof meets idolaters on their premise that distinct deities manage different domains and are worshiped to secure benefits or avert harm.
rows.anchor: فإنهم إنما يعبدون أرباب الأصنام بأصنامهم من جهة تدبيرهم للكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone ultimately manages humans and all other beings, He alone deserves worship and lordship.
rows.anchor: تدبير العالم الإنساني وسائر الموجودات جميعا يقوم به الله سبحانه لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of the arguments is deliberate; without this distinction, the author says one might expect the proofs about the afterlife and truth to precede the proof engaging idolaters.
rows.anchor: ولولا اعتبار هذه النكتة كان الظاهر أن تذكر أولا الحجة الثانية ثم الثالثة ثم الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life first appears to mean the principle enabling knowledge and power; inquiry extends it from animals to plants, whose vital processes disclose life too.
rows.anchor: ثم اكتشف من طريق النظر العلمي أن ذلك لا يختص بأقسام الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More broadly, life is the capacity to yield fitting effects and death their absence; the definition applies to earth, actions, words, and the human being.
rows.anchor: ثم الحياة وهي تقابل الموت الذي هو بطلان مبدأ الأعمال الحيوية تعود بحسب التحليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an calls religion life because true Islam is the divinely created human nature.
rows.anchor: ولذا عد القرآن الشريف الدين حياة للإنسان لأنه يرى أن الدين الحق وهو الإسلام هو الفطرة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On narrower definitions, the expression means an animal, or an animal or plant, coming from nonliving matter and nonliving parts separating from living organisms.
rows.anchor: فعلى النظرتين الأوليين هو خروج الحيوان أو الحيوان والنبات بالكينونة من غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s context favors the broad functional sense: something beneficial or alive emerges from an unproductive or dead source, and the reverse occurs.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية الكريمة بالنظر إلى سياقها ومقام المخاطبة فيها أن يكون المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse counters the idolaters’ argument for separate managing gods by showing that all management, both human-specific and universal, ends with God.
rows.anchor: والآية ترد عليهم حجتهم ببيان انتهاء التدبيرات المختلفة إليه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the questions progress from human sustenance to hearing, sight, and life, “bringing living from dead” here likely means bringing a human life of reason and religion from its opposite.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بإخراج الحي من الميت وبالعكس - والله أعلم - إخراج الإنسان الحي بالسعادة الإنسانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain, plant growth, and sensory powers sustain and let people use provision; without hearing and sight, people would fail to benefit and perish.
rows.anchor: { أمن يملك السمع والأبصار } منكم فتتم بهما فائدة رزقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final question about who manages all affairs makes the proof universal; the polytheists answer “God,” since they acknowledge His ultimate management.
rows.anchor: فسيقولون الله } اعترافا بأنه الذي ينتهي إليه جميع هذه التدبيرات في الإنسان وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admission entails that God is the true Lord and deserves exclusive worship; if truth and guidance are with Him, worship of other supposed lords is error.
rows.anchor: فإن الهدى مع الحق لا غير فلا يبقى عند غيره الذي هو الباطل إلا الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase compresses paired opposites: beyond truth with guidance lies only falsehood with error.
rows.anchor: فماذا بعد الحق الذي معه الهدى إلا الباطل الذي معه الضلال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some exegetes call the paired omission an ihtibāk: “falsehood” is omitted after “truth,” and “guidance” after “error”; the author prefers his own explanation.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم ان في الآية احتباكا - وهو من المحسنات البديعية -

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers his direct explanation of the concise wording over the alternative rhetorical analysis.
rows.anchor: والوجه هو الذي قدمناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How are you turned away?” asks how long they will turn from truth and guidance toward error.
rows.anchor: إلى متى تصرفون عن الحق الذي معه الهدى إلى الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s decisive sentence that persistent transgressors will not believe realizes their self-chosen turn from truth into error, rather than imposing unbelief arbitrarily.
rows.anchor: إنا لم نقض عدم هدى الفاسقين وعدم إيمانهم ظلما ولا جزافا

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators take “the word” as a sentence of punishment and “they do not believe” as its causal explanation; al-Tabataba’i rejects this as unsound because the analogy is unclear.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالكلمة في الآية كلمة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even necessary truths and laws evident in the created order depend in some way on divine decree rather than existing independently.
rows.anchor: الأمور الضرورية والأحكام والقوانين البينة التي تجري في النظام المشهود

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation attaches “they could not hear or see” to the doubled punishment: they could hear and see but refused to do so.
rows.anchor: في محل النصب بنزع الخافض وهو متعلق بقوله يضاعف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the deaf and blind as the unbelievers’ idols, which cannot hear or see.
rows.anchor: نفي السمع والبصر عن آلهتهم وأوثانهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A third interpretation reads “ما” as duration rather than negation: their punishment lasts as long as they live.
rows.anchor: ليست للنفي بل تجري مجرى قولهم لأواصلنك ما لاح نجم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation treats inability to hear and see as a figure for their aversion to hearing God’s signs and considering them.
rows.anchor: فالكلام على الكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited alternative readings are all weak; the last is the most reasonable among them, but the author’s previously explained reading is the correct one.
rows.anchor: وأعدل الوجوه آخرها وهي جميعا سخيفة ظاهرة السخافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Losing one’s self is a metaphor: God entrusted each person with himself, and disbelief and sin squander that entrusted self.
rows.anchor: فخسران النفس كناية عن الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fabricated deities and claims are imaginary; with worldly life ended, these inventions disappear and the truth becomes manifest.
rows.anchor: وبانطواء بساط الحياة الدنيا يزول وينمحي تلك الأوهام

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’ explains “لا جرم” as originally meaning inevitably or without doubt, then developing into an emphatic “truly” or oath-like expression.
rows.anchor: عن الفراء أن { لا جرم } في الأصل بمعنى لا بد ولا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba’i suggests the phrase may derive from “جرم,” cutting: nothing cuts off the conclusion, so the phrase means “truly.”
rows.anchor: وقد ذكروا أن { جرم } بفتحتين بمعنى القطع فلعلها كانت في الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the greatest losers among the afterlife’s inhabitants because they destroyed themselves through disbelief and have no prospect of salvation while persisting in defiance.
rows.anchor: فلا مطمع في نجاتهم من النار في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second possible comparison is with worldly life: they lose both lives, but the afterlife loss is greater because it is everlasting while this life is brief.
rows.anchor: لكنهم في الآخرة أخسر لكونها دائمة مخلدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds intensify through their consequences in the afterlife; the author prefers the first reading because the verse appears to restrict the greatest losers to them there.
rows.anchor: وأحسن الوجهين أولهما لأن ظاهر الآية حصر الأخسرين فيهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says “خبت” first means low, settled land, then “اخبت” came to mean humility; “the humble” are meek and unproud in worship, and their hearts soften.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الخبت المطمئن من الأرض
